candidate_sources.title: Postharvest Rots of Banana - University of Hawaii CTAHR
candidate_sources.snippet: Extension factsheet covering postharvest diseases of banana including anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum musae. Describes symptoms as black or brown sunken spots on fruit peel with salmon-colored acervuli. Covers disease cycle, conditions favoring infection, and management practices.

candidate_sources.title: Colletotrichum musae (tip rot of banana) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive CABI datasheet on Colletotrichum musae covering identity, distribution, hosts/species affected, diagnosis, biology and ecology, impacts, and prevention/control of banana anthracnose. Describes latent infection in immature fruits with symptoms developing during ripening.

candidate_sources.title: Anthracnose of Banana | Plantix Library - Pests & Diseases
candidate_sources.snippet: Dedicated page on banana anthracnose describing symptoms (sunken dark lesions with orange spore masses on ripening fruit), causal agent Colletotrichum musae, favorable conditions (high humidity, 25-30°C), and integrated management including cultural practices and fungicide application.

candidate_sources.title: Banana Bunchy Top Disease in Hawaii: Symptoms, Diagnosis and Management
candidate_sources.snippet: BBTD is the most serious virus disease of banana worldwide. Initial symptoms consist of dark green streaks (Morse code streaking) in the veins of lower portions of the leaf midrib and petiole. Infected leaves are erect, narrow, stunted with yellow margins. Covers symptoms, diagnosis, aphid vector control, and management strategies.

candidate_sources.title: Banana bunchy top virus (bunchy top of banana) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive datasheet covering identity, distribution, hosts, vectors (Pentalonia nigronervosa), biology and ecology, symptoms, diagnosis, impacts, and prevention/control of Banana bunchy top virus (genus Babuvirus, family Nanoviridae). Key management actions include monitoring plantations for symptoms and rapid removal of diseased plants.

candidate_sources.title: Banana bunchy top (121) - Pacific Pests, Pathogens & Weeds Fact Sheet
candidate_sources.snippet: Fact sheet on banana bunchy top disease covering common and scientific names, symptoms (dark green streaks on leaf veins, stunted narrow leaves, bunched appearance), pathogen biology (circular ssDNA virus transmitted by banana aphid), distribution across Asia-Pacific and Africa, and management including use of virus-free planting material and aphid control.

candidate_sources.title: Key Pests and Pathogens of Banana | BBTV - University of Hawaii CTAHR
candidate_sources.snippet: Banana bunchy top virus (BBTV, genus Babuvirus, family Nanoviridae) causes the most destructive viral disease of banana worldwide. Symptoms include dark green streaks in veins (dot-dash 'Morse code' pattern), stunting, leaf chlorosis and rosetting, progressively shorter and narrower leaves creating a bunched appearance. Transmitted by banana aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa). Covers identification, biology, and integrated pest management.

candidate_sources.title: Banana bunchy top virus (bunchy top of banana) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet covering Identity, Overview, Distribution, Dispersal, Hosts/Species Affected, Vectors & Intermediate Hosts, Diagnosis, Biology & Ecology, Impacts, Prevention/Control for Banana bunchy top virus. The most destructive viral disease of banana and plantain worldwide, restricted to some countries in Africa and the Asia-Pacific region.

candidate_sources.title: Banana bunchy top virus (bunchy top of banana) | PlantWise Plus Knowledge Bank
candidate_sources.snippet: Full datasheet on Banana bunchy top virus. Covers pathogen biology, host range, geographic distribution, symptoms and diagnosis, disease management including removal of infected mats, use of BBTV-free planting material, aphid vector control, and legislative controls on movement of planting material.

candidate_sources.title: Musicillium theobromae (cigar end rot) - CABI Invasive Species Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: Cigar end rot is a fungal disease of banana caused by Musicillium theobromae (syn. Verticillium theobromae). The disease causes dry rot of the flower end producing an ash grey wrinkled lesion similar to the burnt end of a cigar. Covers distribution, hosts, symptoms, biology, management.

candidate_sources.title: Cigar end rot on banana - Plantwise Plus Knowledge Bank
candidate_sources.snippet: Cigar end rot on banana caused by Trachysphaera fructigena and Verticillium theobromae. Black necrosis spreads from the flower into the tip of immature fingers. Management includes removing dead leaves, pruning to reduce humidity, removing floral remains 8-11 days after bunch formation, and minimizing bruising during harvest.

candidate_sources.title: Cigar end rot: Verticillium theobromae - TNAU Agritech Portal
candidate_sources.snippet: Cigar end rot of banana caused by Verticillium theobromae. Symptoms include blackening and folding of banana finger tips giving corrugated ash-covered appearance. Transported via wind or rain splashes. Reported from Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh in India. Disease incidence correlated with rainfall.

candidate_sources.title: Cordana leaf spot | Improving the understanding of banana - ProMusa
candidate_sources.snippet: Cordana leaf spot is caused by Neocordana musae and Neocordana johnstonii. Leaf spots (up to 10 cm) are oval to diamond-shaped and pale brown with a yellow border. Although common worldwide, it has generally little impact on production. Infected leaves should be removed. Contact fungicides like chlorothalonil or mancozeb and systemic fungicides such as tebuconazole are recommended.

candidate_sources.title: Fact sheet - Banana diamond leaf spot (072) - Pacific Pests, Pathogens & Weeds
candidate_sources.snippet: Banana diamond leaf spot caused by Cordana musae. Yellow or pale brown, oval- or eye-shaped spots appear near the leaf margins of lower leaves. Spots enlarge and central area becomes necrotic with concentric zonation. Spores produced in large quantities on the underside of leaves. Spread by splashing water and wind.

candidate_sources.title: Cordana leaf spot | Disease Treatment | Bayer Crop Science
candidate_sources.snippet: Cordana leaf spot (CLS) of banana caused by Neocordana musae and N. johnstonii. Leaf spots are oval to diamond-shaped and pale brown with a yellow border on the upper leaf side. Growth accelerated by frequent rain and hot humid conditions. Luna Experience registered for control. Cavendish bananas appear more tolerant than native species.

candidate_sources.title: Fusarium Wilt or Panama Disease - University of Hawaii CTAHR
candidate_sources.snippet: Key Pests and pathogens of banana in the Pacific. Fusarium Wilt or Panama Disease. Covers symptoms, pathogen biology, races, and integrated pest management for banana Fusarium wilt.

candidate_sources.title: Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense (Panama disease of banana) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet covering Identity, Overview, Distribution, Dispersal, Hosts/Species Affected, Diagnosis, Biology & Ecology, Natural Enemies, Impacts, Prevention/Control for Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. cubense.

candidate_sources.title: Fusarium wilt | Improving the understanding of banana - ProMusa
candidate_sources.snippet: Comprehensive resource on Fusarium wilt of banana covering symptoms, pathogen races including Tropical Race 4, distribution, diagnosis, and management strategies for banana production.

candidate_sources.title: Mycosphaerella fijiensis (black Sigatoka) | CABI Compendium
candidate_sources.snippet: CABI Compendium datasheet covering identity, overview, distribution, dispersal, hosts/species affected, diagnosis, biology & ecology, impacts, prevention/control for Mycosphaerella fijiensis. Black sigatoka is a leaf-spot disease of banana plants caused by the ascomycete fungus Mycosphaerella fijiensis. Found in nearly all banana-growing regions. Can reduce fruit yield by up to 50%.

candidate_sources.title: Black sigatoka - APS Education Center
candidate_sources.snippet: APS plant disease lesson on Black Sigatoka caused by Mycosphaerella fijiensis. Covers symptoms, pathogen biology, disease cycle, and management. Yellow Sigatoka caused by M. musicola produces tiny light yellow specks; Black Sigatoka shows reddish-brown flecks on leaf underside. M. fijiensis produces more ascospores than conidia, reverse is true for M. musicola.

candidate_sources.title: Chapter II | Key Pests and Pathogens of Banana | Black Leaf Streak or Sigatoka Disease
candidate_sources.snippet: University of Hawaii CTAHR extension guidebook chapter on Black Leaf Streak (Sigatoka) disease of banana. Covers symptoms, pathogen identification, disease development and IPM strategies for banana production.
